title: Total mass of the uniform law on disjoint-coordinate vectors
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$, and consider the finite set of vectors $(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ of length $n$ in which each coordinate $x_i$ takes one of the three values *neither*, *left-only*, or *right-only*. Under the uniform probability law on this set, the total mass — the measure assigned to the set of all such vectors — equals $1$.
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive natural number
measure is the uniform law on the finite type of length-n vectors over the three-element coordinate type
the set measured is the whole space (universal set)
replaced: The uniform law on disjoint-coordinate vectors has total mass $1$.
